gloss: proposal; suggestion; coming up with an idea

definitions.gloss: proposal; suggestion; coming up with an idea; initiative
definitions.explanation: The act of conceiving and proposing an idea or plan. Emphasizes the origination of an idea rather than its execution.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは{彼|かれ}の{発案|はつあん}だ。
{社長|しゃちょう}の{発案|はつあん}で{新|あたら}しい{制度|せいど}が{導入|どうにゅう}された。
examples.english: A new system was introduced at the president's initiative.

examples.japanese: {部下|ぶか}からの{発案|はつあん}を{積極的|せっきょくてき}に{取|と}り{入|い}れることで、{職場|しょくば}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}が{良|よ}くなった。
examples.english: By actively adopting suggestions from subordinates, the workplace atmosphere improved.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a suru-verb ({発案|はつあん}する). Often used to credit the origin of an idea or initiative. The person who came up with the idea is the {発案者|はつあんしゃ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {発案|はつあん}する (to propose, to come up with an idea)
- {発案者|はつあんしゃ} (originator, person who proposed)
- 〜の{発案|はつあん}で (at the initiative of ~)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {提案|ていあん}: proposal, suggestion — more formal, emphasizes the act of presenting an idea to others
- {考案|こうあん}: devising, inventing — emphasizes the creative thinking process
